messages.author: 6b13d9fbd0ae7797
messages.subject: Finite Mixture model in binary data
parts:
Hi everyone,
From my understanding, mixture models are meant to work in continuous and count data due to other reason as such as computations of gradient etc. 
1. Does anyone have an idea with an example how to fit a mixture model in binary data? 

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 6037c7a8928be573
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Finite Mixture model in binary data
parts: Just based on my experience with mixture modeling in Stan (and other packages), bernoulli mixtures are very unstable because one of the components will tend to disappear while the other component(s) capture all the variance, even when you have strong reason to believe multiple components exist. You can use the advice on mixture component identification and strong priors to avoid this outcome, but it is harder with binary outcomes to get a reasonable solution, probably because mixtures were designed for modeling continuous outcomes. I would consider even setting hard constraints on the mixing parameters (i.e., 60-40 or 70-30 as the range of possible component mixtures). The great thing about Stan is that you can use a variety of constraint possibilities to get what you're looking for.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Finite Mixture model in binary data
parts:
The problem is just that a Bernoulli mixture reduces to
a single Bernoulli unless there's external structure,
say with mixing ratio lambda in (0, 1) and chances of
success theta[1], theta[2] in (0, 1), for y in { 0, 1 }
we have:

p(y | lambda, theta)

= lambda * bernoulli(y | theta[1])
+ (1 - lambda) * bernoulli(y | theta[2])

= bernoull(y | lambda * theta[1]
+ (1 - lambda) * theta[2])

- Bob
